columns.rationale: distinct_count 3322 equals the dataset row_count of 3322 and null_rate is 0.0, so tailnum uniquely identifies each aircraft record.

Sample values (1956.0, 1959.0, ... 2013.0) are all whole numbers despite the landed DECIMAL(38,9) type, so casting to INTEGER is safe; null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 nulls) means the manufacture year is sometimes missing and is retained as nullable, renamed per operator guidance to spell out the abbreviated name.
null_rate 0.0 with only 3 distinct_values (Fixed wing multi engine, Fixed wing single engine, Rotorcraft) covering plane type as documented by the operator.
null_rate 0.0 across 35 distinct manufacturers as recorded verbatim by the FAA registry, e.g. samples AGUSTA SPA, AIRBUS, BEECH, BOEING.
null_rate 0.0 across 127 distinct models as recorded by the registry, e.g. samples 150, 172E, 310Q, 550.
distinct_values [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0] are all whole numbers with null_rate 0.0, so the engine count casts safely from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.
samples 2.0 through 12.0 and max 450.0 are all whole numbers with null_rate 0.0, so the seat count casts safely from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER.

distinct_values (90.0 to 432.0) are whole numbers and the operator confirms this is average cruising speed in mph, but null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows) means the column is sparsely populated and is retained as nullable; renamed with the mph unit suffix per operator convention.
null_rate 0.0 across 6 distinct engine types (4 Cycle, Reciprocating, Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet, Turbo-prop, Turbo-shaft).
is_airbyte_metadata is true; this is a capture-tool surrogate identifier, not a business column.
is_airbyte_metadata is true; distinct_count 1 shows a single extraction timestamp (2026-09-02T23:26:22), a pipeline artifact rather than business data.
is_airbyte_metadata is true; distinct_count 1 with value '{}' shows an empty capture-tool metadata blob.

decisions.rationale: tailnum has distinct_count 3322 equal to row_count 3322 with null_rate 0.0, so it alone identifies each aircraft record.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 3322, so no exact-duplicate removal is required.
year has null_rate 0.021072 (70 of 3322 rows); nulls are retained rather than imputed or dropped.
speed has null_rate 0.993076 (3299 of 3322 rows), making it sparsely populated but still retained as nullable rather than dropped.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning.

purpose: silver_planes is a cleaned, per-aircraft reference table derived from the bronze FAA aircraft registry snapshot (nyc_planes), reduced to the tail numbers observed among 2013 NYC flights, intended to be joined with flight-level silver tables for aircraft attribute enrichment.
usage: Join downstream flight tables to this table on tailnum to attach manufacturer, model, type, engine, seat, and performance attributes; consumers should expect manufacture_year to be null for a small share of rows and speed_mph to be null for nearly all rows, and must handle these nulls explicitly rather than assume completeness.
limitations: speed_mph is null for 99.3% of rows (3299 of 3322), making it unsuitable for aggregate speed analysis without heavy caveats; manufacture_year is null for 2.1% of rows (70 of 3322); per operator context, aircraft operated by American Airlines and Envoy Air are entirely absent from this registry extract because those carriers reported fleet numbers rather than tail numbers.
